cohort: 8,658 women with one previous cesarean and at least one risk factor (BMI ≥30, hypertension, or diabetes) from a population of 280,882 births in Ohio during 2006 and 2007
finding: Although high-risk women with one prior cesarean are less likely to attempt a trial of labor after cesarean, those who do have a high VBAC success rate, with prior vaginal delivery, lower pregnancy weight gain, Caucasian race, and labor augmentation being positive predictors.
mod_finding: The study found that high-risk women with one prior cesarean section who attempted a trial of labor after cesarean had a high rate of successful vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC).
